title: Language model beats billing codes at reconstructing pregnancy episodes from notes
summary: A large language model given chronologically concatenated clinical notes and messages identified pregnancy episodes and extracted gestational age, outcome, assisted-reproduction treatment and complications for 30 patients with 74 pregnancies. On a held-out set of 20 patients (54 pregnancies), checked against manual chart review, it found 53 pregnancies with 3 spurious episodes, against 40 found and 24 spurious for a hierarchical ICD-code algorithm (F1 0.96 versus 0.68), with median absolute start-date error 0 versus 25.5 days. The authors state that the two methods used different input data, so the gain reflects both the information in notes and the model; this is a single-health-system proof of concept in a preprint.
ai_technology: A large language model (GPT-5) extracts pregnancy episodes, dates, outcomes and complications from unstructured clinical notes.
organization: University of California, San Francisco; U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research

evidence.tested: Retrospective comparison with manual chart review on 20 held-out patients covering 54 pregnancies.
evidence.unknown: Note content and model contribution cannot be separated; small single-institution sample; not peer reviewed; larger multi-institutional evaluation not done.
evidence.ai_role: The language model identified and characterized pregnancy episodes from clinical notes.
